title: Charging an EV in 5 Minutes Is Real. But There's a Catch #shorts

scenes.text: Charge an electric car in five minutes? It's real. It's in China right now.
BYD's new flash chargers push up to fifteen hundred kilowatts. Ten to seventy percent in about five minutes, nearly full in nine.
The trick: a thousand volts, up to fifteen hundred amps, and a battery built to take it.
Here's the catch. Fifteen hundred kilowatts is about what a thousand American homes use on average, from one plug.
So stations hide their own batteries. They sip from the grid, then dump energy into your car. A few cars back to back can drain them.
And your car must be built for a thousand volts. Still, BYD says it passed ten thousand stations in August.
Five minutes to charge. Would that make you give up gas? Follow EV Drive.
